title: Predict how by-value parameters and ref, out, or in affect caller storage

rubric.point: Explains that `in` makes `value` a readonly alias of `total`'s storage rather than a copy of 5. Readonly only blocks writes through `value`, so the write to `total` is visible when `value` is read.

questions.model:
It prints **20**. The `in` parameter is a by-reference alias of the variable `total`, not a copy of its value at the time of the call. Readonly means only that `Report` cannot assign through `value`. Other code can still change the underlying storage, so after `total = 20` the alias reads 20.

*(Optional: without `in`, `value` would be a copy and the program would print 5.)*

options: 20, because each class parameter receives its own copy of the object, so neither write in the method reaches the object that acct refers to
45, because both parameters hold copies of one reference: the write through target changes the shared object, and rebinding target leaves source on it
95, because both parameters alias the same caller variable, so rebinding target also moves source to the new object before the final write
90, because assigning a new object to a class parameter replaces the caller's reference in acct, so acct now refers to the new object

rubric.point: Chooses 45: the write through target mutates the object shared with source and acct, and reassigning target rebinds only that local reference, so source still adds 5 to the original object.

questions.model: **45.** Each by-value parameter is a separate copy of the same reference. `target.Balance = 40` changes the object that `source` and `acct` also refer to. Assigning `new Account` rebinds only `target`, so `source.Balance += 5` still updates the original object: 40 + 5 = 45.
